outcome: No result since 26 January 2024 addresses the infinitude of balanced primes; the conjecture remains open with no known proof, disproof, or targeted partial result.
summary: Balanced primes are primes equal to the arithmetic mean of the nearest prime above and below (e.g. 5, 53, 157, ...; OEIS A006562). It is conjectured, but not proven, that infinitely many exist. Searching for work since 26 January 2024, I found: (1) the current Wikipedia article on balanced primes, which cites no post-2024 progress on infinitude and whose most recent factual update concerns a 2023 record for a related but distinct object (largest known CPAP-3, three primes in arithmetic progression); (2) the OEIS sequence A006562 page, which received several comments in 2024-2025 — M. F. Hasler (2024-10-15) noted a characterization via vanishing second differences of the prime sequence, Peter Schorn (2025-04-30) restated the definition, and Alain Rocchelli (2024-03-21 and 2024-03-23) proposed two asymptotic-density conjectures about the growth rate and average spacing of balanced primes. None of these is a proof or disproof of infinitude, and none is even a restriction of the infinitude question to a special case (a 'case' in the sense of §3.1) — the Rocchelli conjectures are themselves unproven conjectures about a different quantity (asymptotic density/gap growth), so even if they were later proven they would not by themselves settle whether the set is infinite. Per the deep-dive rules (§3.1), an existence/infinitude question moves only when it is answered; density conjectures, definitional restatements, and record-largest-example searches do not narrow whether an answer exists. I also checked for any AI involvement broadly in prime-related work during this period (searches surfaced OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra work on largest known prime gaps, and general LLM-mathematics survey pages), but nothing in that AI-related work touches balanced primes specifically — it concerns a different, unrelated prime-gap record problem. I found no arXiv preprint, announcement, or forum discussion since January 2024 claiming progress specifically on the infinitude of balanced primes.
competing_reading: One could argue the OEIS comment activity (Hasler's second-difference characterization, Rocchelli's density conjectures) constitutes 'progress' in a loose sense, since it deepens the theoretical framing of the sequence. But under the scope rule in §3.1, these are restatements or entirely new, still-open conjectures about a different quantity (density/spacing), not a narrowing of the infinitude question itself, so they do not qualify as `progress` or `partial`.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof that the set of balanced primes is infinite (e.g., via a density/heuristic argument made rigorous, or a sieve-theoretic result specifically targeting this equal-gap condition), or a rigorous proof of one of Rocchelli's density conjectures that, as a corollary, implies infinitude.
